{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — verified findings and negotiation posture

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2. The Agreement is materially thin on customer protections and carries three critical gaps and three walk-away items.

Most significantly, the Agreement contains **no indemnification, no intellectual property or data ownership provision, and no limitation of liability**. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site, supplies the software and hosting environment, and holds our Content, customer information and Confidential Information — yet nothing vests ownership of the deliverables, Content or Site customer data in us, nothing obliges HDI to defend us against third-party IP or data-security claims, and both parties face unlimited direct and consequential liability. There is also no performance warranty, no transition assistance or data return on exit, and no vendor insurance covenant.

On the commercial terms, the risk allocation is one-sided against us. Section 6.1 imposes an open-ended exclusive-dealing and non-compete restraint on the Company across "substantially similar" products for a term that auto-renews annually, with no performance-based exit. Section 4.2 imposes a Customer-payable Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — more than a full year of actual fees under the Section 3.1 revenue share — triggered by *any* Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal and termination for HDI's own breach, while HDI may walk on the same 90 days' notice for nothing.

Two areas are already compliant and require no redline: there is no most-favoured-nation obligation burdening us (the only MFN-style language in §1.8 runs in our favour), and no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binds the Company.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue and position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 | No indemnity, hold-harmless or defence language anywhere; §9 covers only corporate authority and the Globix carve-out. Insert mutual indemnities in §9: HDI covers third-party IP claims, breach of law, data/Content security incidents and wilful misconduct; our indemnity limited to Content and Marks we supply. Placement in §9 preserves survival under §10.7. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 | No IP or data ownership provision. §5.2 gives us only artistic/editorial control. Insert new §5.5 vesting ownership of Site deliverables, Content and Site customer data in the Company, HDI retaining its pre-existing platform with a licence-back and no joint ownership. Fallback: HDI owns the build subject to a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free licence to us. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | No cap or damages exclusion; unlimited exposure on both sides, including HDI as host of our Content and Confidential Information. Add mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with our payment obligations outside the cap. Place as §9(c) to survive termination. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | §6.1 restrains the Company for the whole (annually auto-renewing) term across Deerskin Products and loosely defined "substantially similar" products, with no performance exit (§1.6 covers only late launch). Fallback taken: limit to Deerskin Products for 12 months from the Effective Date, terminating automatically on HDI's launch or service failure. HDI's reciprocal covenants (§6.3) left intact. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | §4.2 Termination Payment (50% of trailing 12-month Net Sales above $800,000) exceeds a full year of actual fees and is triggered by any Company termination, including non-renewal and termination for HDI's breach; HDI pays nothing on its own exit. Cap at three months' §3.1 fees, make it the sole monetary remedy, and disapply where we terminate for HDI's breach or under §1.6. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | §6.1 also operates as a field-of-use/non-compete covering competitor product lines and our other channels and sourcing decisions; the §6.2 closeout carve-out is too narrow. Delete the Company-side covenant, retaining HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" branded site. Fallback: restrict to Deerskin Products, term-only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 | §4.1 gives HDI a symmetrical 90-day convenience right during a renewing term, and §4.2 penalises our exit. Give the Company a 30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid fees, limit HDI to end-of-term non-renewal on 90 days' notice, and delete §4.2(a)–(c). Fallback: cap at three months' fees. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 | §10.3 is a bare successors clause: no affiliate/M&A carve-out for us and no restriction on HDI, which could assign to a competitor. Add our affiliate/successor carve-out, require our consent (not unreasonably withheld) for HDI assignments with a competitor bar, and confirm a Company change of control is not an assignment and gives HDI no termination or re-pricing right. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | §1.4 grants access to HDI's systems and Content tools to "the Company" only, silent on duration and revocability. Extend to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, tie revocation to termination or our uncured material breach, and confirm transfer to a successor. Fallback: affiliate coverage on written notice plus M&A successor transfer. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Missing | § 5.4 | §9 contains only corporate authority reps and the Globix acknowledgement; no workmanlike-services, specification-conformance, legal-compliance or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Add §9(c) with a 12-month Site conformance period and re-perform/repair/refund remedy. Fallback: 90 days. No existing disclaimer to displace. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 | §4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment; no migration assistance, data return, deletion or certification, and §10.7 survival does not cure this. Insert new §4.3: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and customer/order data within 30 days in machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification. Fallback: 90 days' assistance. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Deviation | § 1.4 | No minimum purchase or volume cap (fees accrue only on actual Net Sales above $11,000/month), but §4.2(a) is a take-or-pay charge on exit payable in eight quarterly instalments for services never received. Fallback taken: convert to a true-up capped at HDI's documented unrecovered Site costs and disapply where we terminate for HDI's non-performance or failure to launch under §1.6. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 | §4.1 auto-renews for one-year terms (acceptable length) but requires 90 days' non-renewal notice with no renewal reminder. Shorten to 30 days and require an HDI reminder 60 days before each anniversary. Fallback: 60-day window. No fee escalator, so no uplift cap needed. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | §3.4 already provides 30 days' notice, our business hours, HDI-borne cost and payment-records-only scope, but has no frequency limit, confidentiality requirement or systems-access restriction. Limit to once per 12 months, confine to off-site review of copies, bar access to our systems, networks and facilities, and confirm §8 confidentiality treatment. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 | New York law matches our position and there is no arbitration clause, but the clause omits forum selection. Add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the existing sentence intact. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 | The only most-favoured-treatment language (§1.8) runs in our favour; §3.1 has no benchmarking or price-matching mechanic and §7.1 cross-promotion is mutual. No redline proposed. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 | No personnel covenant anywhere; §5.4's appointed-representative provisions impose no hiring restraint. Already at our preferred position; no redline needed. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 | No insurance provision, despite HDI hosting the Site, processing orders and export files and accessing Content and user data. Insert new §10.9: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These three findings sit at the playbook's walk-away threshold and should be resolved before signature:

1. **No vendor IP indemnity (INDEMN, critical).** The absence of any HDI defence and indemnity — in an agreement where HDI supplies the software, technology and hosting environment and handles our Content and customer information — is the playbook walk-away position.
2. **Open-ended exclusive dealing on the Company (EXCLUSIVITY, high).** §6.1 restrains us for the full, annually auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit, matching the playbook's walk-away pattern. We propose the fallback (Deerskin Products, 12 months, automatic termination on HDI performance failure) given HDI's reciprocal covenants in §6.3.
3. **Customer-payable Termination Payment quantum (LD, high).** §4.2 exceeds a full year of actual fees and remaining contract value, applies to ordinary non-renewal and to termination for HDI's own breach, and is entirely one-way. We propose a three-month fee cap and disapplication on HDI breach rather than deletion, recognising that HDI funds Site development and recoups through the revenue share.

We also treat the two remaining criticals — **absent IP/data ownership** and **absent limitation of liability** — as must-fix. We should not sign an agreement in which a vendor hosts our customer data with no ownership provision and unlimited exposure on both sides.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** implementing the proposals above, sequenced so that the three criticals (indemnity in §9, ownership in new §5.5, liability cap as §9(c)) and the three walk-away items lead the cover note.
2. **Confirm the commercial baseline** with the business team: trailing Net Sales and monthly run-rate, so we can quantify the §4.2 exposure and pressure-test the three-month fee cap and the USD 1,000,000 liability floor.
3. **Agree the fallback ladder internally** before the first call: 12-month/Deerskin-only exclusivity; three-month cap (or cost true-up) on the Termination Payment; HDI-owned build with a perpetual royalty-free licence; 90-day transition assistance; 60-day non-renewal window; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
4. **Ask HDI two diligence questions:** the hosting and data-security arrangements (including the Globix relationship referenced in §9) and its current insurance certificates, to support the new §10.9 covenant.
5. **Preserve drafting placement** — indemnity, warranty and cap inside §9 and the transition clause as new §4.3 — to avoid renumbering and to capture the existing §10.7 survival.
6. **No action** on MFN (§1.8) or non-solicitation; both are already at our preferred position."}
